newsitem.title: FRANCE: IMF's Camdessus, Chirac to review debt initiative.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus, Chirac to review debt initiative.

text.p: IMF managing director Michel Camdessus will review progress on a debt initiative to help the world's poor heavily indebted countries in talks with French President Jacques Chirac on Tuesday, French officials said on Monday.

France has strongly pushed the initiative -- in which the International Monetary Fund, World Bank and Paris Club of creditor nations are meant to act jointly in providing debt relief -- as a way of helping its former African colonies.
The first beneficiary, however, is likely to be former British colony Uganda, a country which has clashed with French interests in central Africa, officials said.
They said Ivory Coast, Burkina Faso and Bolivia were among those next in line.
French officials said France was keen to ensure the criteria for granting debt relief were flexible enough to apply to as many countries as possible.
Ivory Coast, France's senior ally in West Africa, is not technically poor enough to qualify for improved debt relief though Paris has promised to support its case.

French officials played down suggestions that plans to give Uganda improved debt relief might be delayed because of an increase in the country's military spending, which diplomats said reflected its alleged support for rebels in eastern Zaire.
Diplomats attending a meeting of African finance officials in Addis Ababa last week said there was concern about a rise in Uganda's military spending.

France regards the former British colony as the main sponsor of Tutsi-dominated movements in Rwanda, Burundi and Zaire, including the rebels who have captured more than a quarter of Zairean territory.
Paris is the main backer of Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko.
